question.problem: Consider the equation $\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡3x-1=0$ for ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$ If the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4},{x}_{5},{x}_{6}$ are written in ascending order, what is the numerical value of ${x}_{2}+{x}_{4}?$
question.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

First, we rearrange the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡3x-1 & =0 \\ \sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡3x & =1 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡3x & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡3x & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}3x & ={45}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}, & \, & \, & 3x & ={135}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{45}^{∘}}{3}+\frac{n\cdot {360}^{∘}}{3} & \, & \, & x & =\frac{{135}^{∘}}{3}+\frac{n\cdot {360}^{∘}}{3} \\ x & ={15}^{∘}+n\cdot {120}^{∘} & \, & \, & x & ={45}^{∘}+n\cdot {120}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x={15}^{∘}$ and $x={45}^{∘}$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x={135}^{∘}$ and $x={165}^{∘}$

- Setting $n=2$ gives $x={255}^{∘}$ and $x={285}^{∘}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$ So, the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4},{x}_{5},{x}_{6}$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x={15}^{∘},{45}^{∘},{135}^{∘},{165}^{∘},{255}^{∘},{285}^{∘}.
$$

Finally, since ${x}_{2}={45}^{∘}$ and ${x}_{4}={165}^{∘},$ we have

$$
{x}_{2}+{x}_{4}=45+165=210.
$$
